```{r}
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(modelsummary)
LongPanelPropj = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelPropj.csv")
LongPanelProp = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelProp.csv")
PanelLong = read_csv("d:/PositStuff/gmpanel/LongPanelProp.csv")
p1=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=graduate/(graduate+not_graduate),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Graduates")+theme_light()
p2=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=graduate/(graduate+not_graduate),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Graduates")+theme_dark()
p9=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=routine_manual_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Manual")+theme_light()
p10=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=routine_manual_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Manual")+theme_dark()
p11=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Higher_Managerial")+theme_light()
p12=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Higher_Managerial")+theme_dark()
p13=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=never_worked_long_term_unemployed/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Unemployed")+theme_light()
p14=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=never_worked_long_term_unemployed/(intermediate_occupations+routine_manual_occupations+never_worked_long_term_unemployed+higher_managerial_administrative_professional_occupations),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Unemployed")+theme_dark()
(p2/p1)|(p10/p9)|(p12/p11)|(p14/p13)
p3=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=local_authority_etc/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%LocalAuthority")+theme_light()
p4=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=local_authority_etc/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%LocalAuthority")+theme_dark()
p4/p3
p5=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=owner_occupied/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+ylab("%Owner_occupied")+theme_light()
p6=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=owner_occupied/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%Owner_occupied")+theme_dark()
p6/p5
p7=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=(other_rented+other_tenures)/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=location))+geom_line()+
  ylab("%other_rented+tenures")+theme_light()
p8=ggplot(PanelLong,aes(x=year,y=(other_rented+other_tenures)/(owner_occupied+other_rented+other_tenures+local_authority_etc),colour=factor(gentrified)))+
stat_summary(fun=mean,geom="line")+geom_jitter()+ylab("%other_rented+tenures")+theme_dark()
```

```{r}
#Simon Rudkin Didn't sponsor this I promise, i just found his posters very pretty and wanted to try and make some too#
library(BallMapper)
set.seed(123)
values = LongPanelPropj$GraduateP
points =  LongPanelPropj |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
#One possible heuristic to set epsilon is to calculate common dispersion metrics for points specifically IQR/2(Probable error) and standard deviation
sd(as.matrix(points))
IQR(as.matrix(points))/2
# In our case it turned out that the best representations are generated with e=0.17 or exactly one sd, for robustness its worthwhile to try other values between 0.17 and 0.14
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.01)
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way
ballassign = ball$points_covered_by_landmarks
#Split by gentrificaiion#
Gentonly = filter(LongPanelPropj,gentrified==1)
values = Gentonly$GraduateP
points =  Gentonly |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
ball1 = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way

Gentnot = filter(LongPanelPropj,gentrified==0)
values = Gentnot$GraduateP
points =  Gentnot |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
ball2 = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way

ColorIgraphPlot(ball,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of Gentrification e=0.17,(Grad%)")
ColorIgraphPlot(ball1,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of Gentrifiying areas e=0.17,(Grad%)")
ColorIgraphPlot(ball2,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of non gentrifying areas e=0.17,(Grad%)")
```

```{r}
#WARNING AI Generated Code as I am only learning how to properly add unit time labels to Ball Mapper Graphs#
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Number of nodes
n_nodes <- length(ball$coloring)

# 2. Calculate ball sizes from your ballassign indices
ball_sizes <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, length)

# 3. Generate unit-time labels for each ball
node_labels <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, function(indices) {
  subset_data <- PanelLong[indices, ]
  paste0(subset_data$location, "-", subset_data$year, collapse = "\n")
})

# 4. Build the vertices data frame safely
vertices_df <- data.frame(
  name = 1:n_nodes,
  label = node_labels,
  coloring = ball$coloring,
  size = ball_sizes
)

# 5. Create the igraph object
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = ball$edges, vertices = vertices_df, directed = FALSE)
#Though I did customise the plot below though#
ggraph(g, layout = "stress") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.8, color = "gray60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = size, color = coloring)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = label), repel = TRUE, size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option="D") +
  theme_light() +
  labs(title = "Ball Mapper Graph of gentrification - points in the same ball are closest on housing market makeup within +-17 percentage points",
       color = "%Graduates", size = "Ball Size(number of points)") + scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 10))
```

```{r}
#Simon Rudkin Didn't sponsor this I promise, i just found his posters very pretty and wanted to try and make some too#
library(BallMapper)
set.seed(123)
values = LongPanelPropj$manualP
points =  LongPanelPropj |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.01)
ball = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way
ballassign = ball$points_covered_by_landmarks
#Split by gentrificaiion#
Gentonly = filter(LongPanelPropj,gentrified==1)
values = Gentonly$manualP
points =  Gentonly |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
ball1 = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way

Gentnot = filter(LongPanelPropj,gentrified==0)
values = Gentnot$manualP
points =  Gentnot |> select(owner_occupiedP,local_authority_etcP,otherrented_tenuresP)
ball2 = BallMapper::BallMapper(as.data.frame(points),as.data.frame(values),epsilon = 0.17) #epsilon 0.17 seems to preserve the complexity in the best way

ColorIgraphPlot(ball,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of Gentrification e=0.17,(Grad%)")
ColorIgraphPlot(ball1,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of Gentrifiying areas e=0.17,(Grad%)")
ColorIgraphPlot(ball2,showLegend = TRUE) + title("Ball Map of non gentrifying areas e=0.17,(Grad%)")
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Number of nodes
n_nodes <- length(ball$coloring)

# 2. Calculate ball sizes from your ballassign indices
ball_sizes <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, length)

# 3. Generate unit-time labels for each ball
node_labels <- sapply(ball$points_covered_by_landmarks, function(indices) {
  subset_data <- PanelLong[indices, ]
  paste0(subset_data$location, "-", subset_data$year, collapse = "\n")
})

# 4. Build the vertices data frame safely
vertices_df <- data.frame(
  name = 1:n_nodes,
  label = node_labels,
  coloring = ball$coloring,
  size = ball_sizes
)

# 5. Create the igraph object
g <- graph_from_data_frame(d = ball$edges, vertices = vertices_df, directed = FALSE)
#Though I did customise the plot below though#
ggraph(g, layout = "stress") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.8, color = "gray60") +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = size, color = coloring)) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = label), repel = TRUE, size = 2.5, color = "black") +
  scale_color_gradient(high="orange",low="darkblue") +
  theme_light() +
  labs(title = "Ball Mapper Graph of gentrification - points in the same ball are closest on housing market makeup within +-17 percentage points",
       color = "%ManualWork", size = "Ball Size(number of points)") + scale_size_continuous(range = c(4, 10))
```
